entities.name: order
entities.description: Single delivered order (Northstar Weekender Pack, originalAmount=100), observed independently and identically at reset-state across all three source runs (refund-rerun, cancel-demo, return-demo). Same order id, product and originalAmount in every source's initial GET /api/order response.

observed_transitions.note: The ONLY action of the four whose availableActions leaves requestRefund=true after completion. cancel_order and request_refund both correctly set requestRefund/cancelOrder/requestPriceAdjustment all to false after their own completion; request_price_adjustment does not reciprocally disable requestRefund.

inferred_relationships.statement: cancel_order and request_refund are mutually exclusive with each other and with request_price_adjustment (each disables the other two upon completion).

request_price_adjustment is NOT mutually exclusive with request_refund server-side, despite the UI's shared messaging ("Price protection is not available while another order request is active") implying all three actions are members of one mutually-exclusive group.
derived_from: return-demo observed_transitions (availableActions.requestRefund remains true after price-adjustment; UI button "Request refund" is still rendered and clickable in return-demo final_snapshot)

contradictions.description: The UI's price-protection unavailability message ("Price protection is not available while another order request is active", shown identically in refund-rerun step 4 and cancel-demo step 4) implies a single shared 'one active order request' invariant across cancellation, refund and price adjustment. But the return-demo recording shows the reverse direction is NOT enforced: after price-adjustment completes, refund remains fully available (both in the API's availableActions and in the rendered UI button). This is an asymmetric/incomplete implementation of the intended mutual-exclusion invariant.

assumptions: Each source run started from an identical reset order state (id 1042, originalAmount 100, all statuses at baseline) based on matching initial GET /api/order responses across all three sources; recordings are NOT one continuous session and object bindings/timestamps differ per source.
No authentication/session mechanism was observed in any source; the app is treated as single-principal for this analysis.
